request: why does stopping distance grow so fast with speed?

beats.intent: A road with a car and two stretches: thinking distance 9 m then braking distance 14 m at 30 mph
beats.narration: At thirty miles an hour, you travel nine metres while you react, then fourteen more while braking: twenty three metres.
beats.code:
stage.title("Stopping distances")
road = Line([-6, -0.8, 0], [6, -0.8, 0], color=GREY_B)
stage.play(Create(road))
stage.add(road)
k = 0.11
think = Rectangle(width=9 * k, height=0.35, stroke_width=0, fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-6 + 9 * k / 2, -0.55, 0])
brake = Rectangle(width=14 * k, height=0.35, stroke_width=0, fill_color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(think, RIGHT, buff=0)
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(think, LEFT))
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(brake, LEFT))
stage.add(think, brake)
stage.label(brake, "30 mph: 23 m", direction=UP, color=WHITE)

beats.intent: Rows for 50 mph (15 + 38 = 53 m) and 70 mph (21 + 75 = 96 m) below
beats.narration: At fifty it is fifteen plus thirty eight: fifty three metres. At seventy, twenty one plus seventy five: ninety six.
beats.code:
rows = []
for y, t, b_, txt in ((-1.8, 15, 38, "50 mph: 53 m"), (-2.8, 21, 75, "70 mph: 96 m")):
    th = Rectangle(width=t * k, height=0.35, stroke_width=0, fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-6 + t * k / 2, y, 0])
    br = Rectangle(width=b_ * k, height=0.35, stroke_width=0, fill_color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(th, RIGHT, buff=0)
    stage.play(GrowFromEdge(th, LEFT), run_time=0.5)
    stage.play(GrowFromEdge(br, LEFT), run_time=0.8)
    stage.add(th, br)
    stage.label(br, txt, direction=UP)
stage.caption("yellow: thinking, red: braking")

beats.narration: Thinking distance grows in step with speed, but braking distance grows with speed squared: more than doubling the speed more than quintuples the braking.

beats.code:
stage.title("The Sierpinski triangle")
A, B, C = np.array([-3.2, -2.6, 0]), np.array([3.2, -2.6, 0]), np.array([0, 2.9, 0])
level = [(A, B, C)]
shapes = VGroup(*[Polygon(*t, stroke_width=1, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8) for t in level])
stage.play(FadeIn(shapes))
stage.add(shapes)

beats.intent: Its middle cut out, leaving 3 triangles, then each of those cut again, leaving 9
beats.narration: Cut out the middle triangle, leaving three. Do the same to each of those: nine.
beats.code:
for step in range(2):
    level = [t for a, b, c in level for t in ((a, (a + b) / 2, (a + c) / 2), ((a + b) / 2, b, (b + c) / 2), ((a + c) / 2, (b + c) / 2, c))]
    new = VGroup(*[Polygon(*t, stroke_width=1, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8) for t in level])
    stage.play(Transform(shapes, new))
stage.caption("3, then 9 triangles")

beats.intent: After more steps, 243 tiny triangles, beside area × 3/4 each step
beats.narration: Keep going forever. Each step keeps three quarters of the area, so the area shrinks towards nothing, yet the pattern never ends.
beats.code:
for step in range(3):
    level = [t for a, b, c in level for t in ((a, (a + b) / 2, (a + c) / 2), ((a + b) / 2, b, (b + c) / 2), ((a + c) / 2, (b + c) / 2, c))]
new = VGroup(*[Polygon(*t, stroke_width=0.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8) for t in level])
stage.play(Transform(shapes, new))
stage.equation(r"\text{area} \times \left(\tfrac34\right)^n \to 0")
stage.caption("243 triangles after 5 steps")

request: how does a rocket move in space with nothing to push against?

beats.intent: A rocket drawn as a tall rectangle with a pointed nose and fins
beats.narration: A rocket in space has no ground or air to push on.
beats.code:
stage.title("How a rocket moves")
body = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=2.4, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to([0, 0.2, 0])
nose = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).scale(0.46).next_to(body, UP, buff=0)
fins = VGroup(Polygon([-0.4, -1.0, 0], [-0.8, -1.4, 0], [-0.4, -0.5, 0], color=RED, fill_opacity=0.6),
              Polygon([0.4, -1.0, 0], [0.8, -1.4, 0], [0.4, -0.5, 0], color=RED, fill_opacity=0.6))
rocket = VGroup(body, nose, fins)
stage.play(FadeIn(rocket))
stage.add(rocket)

beats.intent: Hot gas shooting down out of the bottom, with a big down arrow
beats.narration: It throws hot gas out of the back, very fast. It pushes the gas down...
beats.code:
gas = VGroup(*[Dot([x, -1.2, 0], radius=0.07, color=ORANGE) for x in np.linspace(-0.3, 0.3, 5)])
stage.add(gas)
stage.play(gas.animate.shift(2.0 * DOWN).set_opacity(0.3), run_time=1.2)
down = Arrow([1.4, -1.0, 0], [1.4, -2.8, 0], buff=0, color=ORANGE)
stage.play(GrowArrow(down))
stage.add(down)
stage.label(down, "push on gas", direction=RIGHT, color=ORANGE)

beats.intent: An equal up arrow on the rocket and the rocket rising
beats.narration: ...and the gas pushes the rocket up just as hard. Every push has an equal push back.
beats.code:
up = Arrow([-1.4, -1.0, 0], [-1.4, 0.8, 0], buff=0, color=GREEN)
stage.play(GrowArrow(up))
stage.add(up)
stage.label(up, "push on rocket", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)
stage.play(rocket.animate.shift(0.8 * UP), run_time=1.2)
stage.caption("equal and opposite pushes")

request: how much does it cost to run a 2 kW heater for 3 hours?

beats.intent: A heater box labelled 2 kW with a clock showing 3 hours
beats.narration: A two kilowatt heater runs for three hours.
beats.code:
stage.title("Running cost")
heater = draw_rectangle(stage, width=2.4, height=1.4, color=ORANGE, fill=0.4)
heater.move_to([-3, 0, 0])
stage.label(heater, "2 kW", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)
clock = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE).move_to([2.5, 0, 0])
hand = Line(clock.get_center(), clock.get_center() + 0.6 * RIGHT, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=5)
stage.play(Create(clock), Create(hand))
stage.add(clock, hand)
stage.label(clock, "3 hours", direction=UP)

beats.intent: The picture beside 2 kW × 3 h = 6 kWh
beats.narration: Energy is power times time: two kilowatts for three hours is six kilowatt hours, the units on your bill.

beats.intent: Bars of cost: £1.80 at 30p a kWh against £0.60 for a 0.5 kW fan in the same time
beats.narration: At thirty pence a unit, that is one pound eighty. A half-kilowatt fan for the same three hours costs sixty pence.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [1.80, 0.60], labels=["2 kW heater", "0.5 kW fan"], color=ORANGE)
stage.caption("£ for 3 hours at 30p per kWh")
